hero.title: Mapping Earth's Forest Biomass From Space
hero.description: LEAF LAB develops cutting-edge spaceborne lidar methods to quantify global forest biomass and carbon stocks — connecting satellites to ground truth at planetary scale.

mission.label: Our Mission
mission.title: Forests as the Planet Carbon Ledger
mission.text1: LEAF LAB — Lidar for Ecosystem Analysis and Forest Aboveground Biomass Laboratory — is a research group at the University of Maryland's Department of Geographical Sciences. We use novel remote sensing technologies to understand how forests occupy space and how that links to global carbon stocks and cycles.
mission.text2: Our work spans algorithm development for forest biomass mapping, ecological theory testing, and validation frameworks for international biomass products — bridging fundamental science with climate policy.

cards.title: Spaceborne Lidar
cards.text: GEDI and ICESat-2 missions deliver unprecedented 3-D forest structure data at global scale.

cards.title: Global Biomass
cards.text: Building and validating allometric models for tropical, boreal, and temperate forests.

cards.title: Forest Ecology
cards.text: Testing ecological theory — structural diversity, biodiversity links, disturbance dynamics.

cards.title: Data Fusion
cards.text: Integrating lidar with Landsat, SAR, and optical datasets for multi-scale analysis.

highlights.title: Global Biomass Density Models
highlights.text: Led development of the allometric models behind NASA GEDI footprint-level aboveground biomass density product — the first space-borne lidar designed specifically for forest carbon estimation.

highlights.title: Forests That Guard the Climate
highlights.text: First-of-its-kind GEDI analysis demonstrating that protected areas store significantly more carbon than unprotected forests — direct evidence for nature-based climate solutions.

highlights.title: Charcoal Degradation Mapping
highlights.text: Combined GEDI and Landsat time series to quantify biomass loss from charcoal production across Mozambique — revealing invisible carbon emissions from forest degradation.

cta.label: Join Our Community
cta.title: Interested in forest carbon science?
cta.text: We welcome collaborators, prospective graduate students, and postdoctoral researchers passionate about remote sensing and global forest ecology.
